summary: ING's campaign pages score 0.41 on positioning - traditional in style but leaning towards the challengers - and their defining traits are intensity: the most urgency and deadline language in the set (4.0 against a peer mean of 0.64) and the most persuasion techniques (5.0 against 1.67), on pages that are far longer (about 11,148.67 px against 6,411.72 px) and brighter than peers. Its clearest strengths are clarity of the offer (5.0 against 3.97) and making the offer feel worth having (1.0 against 0.59). Two caveats frame everything below: the compared pages span six different product families, so cross-bank differences are partly product differences rather than communication differences, and no performance data exists in this project, so every recommendation here is a hypothesis to test rather than a cause.

recommendations.title: Cut urgency and deadline language
recommendations.finding: Urgency and deadline language is ING's single largest divergence from the market: 4.0 markers against a peer mean of 0.64, a gap of 3.69 standard deviations, and 2.5 standard deviations above the market on the focus signature.
recommendations.recommendation: Rewrite deadline and countdown phrasing across the campaign pages so that time pressure is replaced by plain statements of what the offer includes and until when it genuinely runs, keeping at most one time-bound element per page.

recommendations.title: Thin out the persuasion stack
recommendations.finding: Persuasion techniques used averages 5.0 on ING's pages against a peer mean of 1.67, a gap of 3.68 standard deviations, with the focus signature 2.5 standard deviations above the market.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep one persuasion device per page - for example a single clearly stated benefit - and remove the stacked remainder, so the offer is argued once instead of several times over.

recommendations.title: Put the conditions next to the 'free' claim
recommendations.finding: "Free" with conditions attached is measured on two thirds of ING's pages (0.67) against a peer mean of 0.23, an above-market rate of free claims that carry qualifications.
recommendations.recommendation: Wherever a page presents an account as free, state the qualifying conditions in the same block as the claim, and move any required small print into that block rather than leaving it to the page footer.

recommendations.title: Shorten the campaign pages
recommendations.finding: Page length averages about 11,148.67 px on ING's pages against a peer mean of 6,411.72 px (gap 1.42 standard deviations), close to double the peer average.
recommendations.recommendation: Cut or collapse repeated sections and bring the offer, its conditions and the call to action into the first screen, treating everything below as supporting detail that has to earn its place.

recommendations.title: Consolidate imagery into fewer, larger visuals
recommendations.finding: ING carries 33 images on average against a peer mean of 19, while the market split shows challenger pages give imagery a much larger share of the page (0.31 against 0.10) and a much larger opening image (0.62 against 0.25) than traditional pages.
recommendations.recommendation: Replace clusters of small supporting images with a smaller number of larger visuals, starting with the opening image, so the page reads as a few deliberate statements rather than many small ones.

recommendations.title: Protect the clear offer while you trim
recommendations.finding: Clarity of the offer is the top-scoring rubric trait at 5.0 against a peer mean of 3.97, and making the offer feel worth having scores 1.0 against a peer mean of 0.59 - the strongest measured traits in ING's profile.
recommendations.recommendation: When cutting length and persuasion, keep exactly the block that carries the offer and the block that makes it feel worth having, and use those two as the test of whether a shortened page still works.

recommendations.title: Back the fast digital sign-up promise with detail
recommendations.finding: Promises fast digital sign-up appears on 0.67 of ING's pages against a peer mean of 0.15, so this is an above-market claim rather than a market-distinguishing one.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep the promise but attach the concrete steps and requirements in the same block - what the customer needs, what happens after they start - so the claim is checkable rather than assertive.

recommendations.title: Keep the mobile-first layout on every campaign page
recommendations.finding: Designed mobile-first scores 1.0 on ING's pages against a peer mean of 0.56, which is a genuine strength rather than a gap.
recommendations.recommendation: Apply the same mobile-first structure to any page still following a desktop-first order, checking that the offer, the conditions and the call to action appear in the same sequence on a phone as on the shortened desktop page.

recommendations.title: Check the digital promise against what ING is in the news for
recommendations.finding: ING's 2 headlines in the 90-day window both fall under the "other" theme, and none under innovation_digital, while the pages put weight on signing up fast and digitally. This is a hypothesis to verify, not evidence that any page or campaign performed.
recommendations.recommendation: On the pages that promise fast digital sign-up, replace generic digital-leadership framing with concrete, checkable detail about the digital journey, so the page does not assert a position the current news coverage does not corroborate.
recommendations.reputation_context: Over 90 days ING has 2 headlines, both themed "other"; no ING headline carried the innovation_digital theme.

recommendations.title: Explain payment limits where the account is described
recommendations.finding: One of ING's two headlines concerns the 5,000 euro daily transfer limit applied by Belgian banks, counted under the "other" theme. Any link between that coverage and what ING's pages say is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: Add a plain-language line about daily transfer limits and the practical conditions of everyday use next to where the account is described, so a visitor meets the operational detail before the marketing claim rather than after it.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING appears in a headline about transfers being limited to 5,000 euro per day across Belgian banks, counted under "other" (2 of 2 ING headlines in the window).

recommendations.title: Review promotional urgency against a regulatory-heavy news period
recommendations.finding: Across the compared banks the 90-day themes lean heavily on regulatory and crisis_or_scandal counts at one large competitor (Belfius: 11 crisis_or_scandal and 9 regulatory headlines out of 26; Revolut: 1 crisis_or_scandal out of 2), while ING's own 2 headlines carry neither theme. Whether promotional deadline framing sits well against that backdrop is a hypothesis to verify, not a measured effect, and the link is not established by this analysis.
recommendations.recommendation: Before adding any new deadline or scarcity framing to account pages, check that the surrounding copy is factual and disclosure-led, and keep promotional timing language away from the blocks that describe fees, limits or conditions.
recommendations.reputation_context: Belfius shows 11 crisis_or_scandal and 9 regulatory headlines over 90 days; Revolut shows 1 crisis_or_scandal. ING's 2 headlines fall under "other".
